summary:
NOMAD (Planet X & SPHEREx Explorer) is an interactive web platform that transforms NASA’s SPHEREx infrared sky survey data into an accessible discovery tool. While SPHEREx maps the entire sky every few months, its public FITS files require specialized calibration and hours of manual frame-by-frame comparison to detect moving objects.
NOMAD solves this by integrating real satellite cutouts and flux measurements from IRSA, stellar astrometry from Gaia DR3, and solar system orbits from JPL Horizons into six intuitive views. Users can visually track celestial drift across epochs, analyze molecular absorption spectra, and classify objects—like brown dwarfs, TNOs, or a hypothetical Planet X candidate—using an audio-fingerprinting-inspired algorithm. Additionally, our self-supervised Tracklet Engine separates genuine moving objects from noise without labeled training data (achieving 93% accuracy on Barnard’s Star) while strictly distinguishing real observations from models.
This democratizes complex space telescope archives for students, citizen scientists, and researchers.
details: NOMAD (Planet X & SPHEREx Explorer) is an interactive web platform that transforms raw, expert-level infrared sky data from NASA’s SPHEREx mission into an accessible visual discovery tool. By integrating live FITS satellite cutouts and flux measurements from IRSA, astrometry from Gaia DR3, and solar system ephemerides from JPL Horizons via Python and JSON pipelines, NOMAD lets users track celestial motion over time, analyze molecular absorption spectra (\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{CH}_4, \text{CO}_2), and classify objects like brown dwarfs, TNOs, or hypothetical Planet X candidates. The project’s core innovation is its cross-disciplinary design: it adapts audio-fingerprinting logic (like Shazam) to match spectral dips and sky motion against a reference database, alongside a custom, self-supervised Tracklet Engine that detects real moving objects across multi-epoch exposures without labeled training data (achieving 93% accuracy on Barnard’s Star). Built with strict scientific transparency—clearly separating empirical observations from modeled curves—NOMAD removes the need for manual frame-by-frame blinking and complex calibration scripts, making real space telescope data immediately explorable for students, citizen scientists, and researchers alike.
